newsitem.title: PERU: Peru urges rebels to free all captives together.
newsitem.headline: Peru urges rebels to free all captives together.

text.p: The Peruvian government is insisting in talks with Marxist rebels that all 74 hostages they are holding be released together, at the same time, government negotiator Domingo Palermo said on Friday.
"My goal is to free the 74 hostages in their entirety, in good health and as quickly as possible," Palermo told a group of foreign correspondents.
Palermo said he was the "contact, not the negotiator, though you could say it is the same thing."

He is in regular touch with both Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, leader of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels in the besieged residence of the Japanese ambassador, and Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori.

He spoke with both Cerpa and Fujimori during a meeting lasting nearly three hours with correspondents from Reuters, the Italian news agency ANSA, Agence France Presse and Mexican TV company ECO. It was his first contact with the press since the Lima hosgtage crisis began more than three weeks ago.
In their radio conversation, Palermo and Cerpa were polite and gentlemanly but reserved.
"How are you? It's a pleasure to hear you Mr. Cerpa," said Palermo.
"At your service, minister," replied Cerpa. "Here we are, and we're not going anywhere."
Cerpa agreed to allow Roman Catholic Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani to return to the residence Sunday to celebrate Mass with the hostages.

A senior government source added that a "guarantor committee" was being set up in the hope of a negotiated solution to the 24-day-old crisis. The committee would consist of members of the government and "two or three very strong institutions or countries," the source said.

Every release of hostages had been coordinated and negotiated between the government and the rebels by radio, by written messages and in one face-to-face meeting between Palermo and Cerpa on Dec. 28, the source said.
Part of the government strategy has been to establish a psychological profile of Cerpa to facilitate talks with him.
"We have seen that he's the classic 'union leader' type...someone who goes to see his boss to ask for a raise of $100 but knowing he will only receive $50 or less," the source said.
"At the beginning he was very aggressive, but now he has calmed down a lot," the source added.

The source said the government was considering moving journalists further from the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence to deny the rebels the chance to get their views out to the world through placards held up to the windows.
The source said the two government ministers still held captive had "an iron will. They want to be the last to leave."
"(Foreign Minister) Francisco Tudela said: 'I want to go out last. Tell the president not to worry'."
The source said that despite early reports that the rebels numbered 20 or more, "we now know there are only about 15 of them inside." He added: "There has been no torture, just a bit of swearing."
